chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered the month of Ramadan for some days and then converted to Islam. He said to me: 'He must make up what was missed.' The approach in this narration is to interpret it as referring to one who converted in the month of Ramadan but did not know that fasting was obligatory upon him, so he fasted (or ate), and then learned afterwards. Indeed, it becomes obligatory upon him to make up (the missed days). This is indicated by his saying 'make up what was missed.' And 'missing' does not occur except after the obligation of the duty has directed towards the accountable person, without the condition of Islam. And one who converts in the month of Ramadan, what passed of it was not directed towards him except by the condition of Islam. And one with this description is not obliged to make up (the fasts) without disagreement.

key_terms.الْمُكَلَّفِ: The accountable person (one subject to religious duties)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a new Muslim who converts during Ramadan regarding the days they missed fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the ruling for a convert who enters Islam during Ramadan after fasting some days, establishing that they must perform qadā (make-up fasting) for those days. The scholar argues that the obligation of fasting is contingent upon the condition of Islam; thus, days prior to conversion were not yet directed toward the individual, making their fasting valid but requiring make-up to fulfill the complete monthly obligation. This reflects the Shia principle that religious duties bind only after the prerequisite conditions are met.
